tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Stonemede Civil Group** is a civil engineering and construction firm that designs and builds bridges, tunnels, and highway interchanges. The company is retiring its aging server room and migrating its project-costing system and structural modeling workloads to virtual machines in Microsoft Azure (Infrastructure as a Service).

**Current Environment:**
- Bid documents, structural drawings, and subcontractor contracts are stored on file servers that will move to Azure virtual machines.
- Site engineers connect from trailers at remote construction sites; head-office staff work from two regional offices.
- A small IT team of six people administers everything, and every IT team member currently holds full administrator rights on every system, at all times.

tabs.title: Migration Requirements
tabs.content:
The Stonemede Civil steering committee has set the following requirements for the migration:
- **Clarify accountability**: Before signing off on the IaaS migration, the committee wants a clear statement of which operational duties transfer to the cloud provider and which remain with Stonemede.
- **Rein in administrative rights**: Administrative access must follow a "just enough, just in time" philosophy so that no one carries standing rights beyond what their current task requires.
- **Harden every layer**: The security lead is mapping each planned control to a layer of a defense-in-depth model, so gaps at any layer become visible.
